newsitem.title: USA: New Yorkers approve, but don't like, Giuliani - poll.
newsitem.headline: New Yorkers approve, but don't like, Giuliani - poll.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani's approval rating hit an all-time high and New Yorkers are likely to re-elect him, though they do not think he is likable or cooperative, a poll said.

The Republican mayor's overall approval rating climbed to 62 percent vs 32 percent, with 84 percent vs 12 percent of the 845 New York City residents surveyed by Quinnipiac College saying he has "strong leadership qualities."

Maurice Carroll, director of Quinnipiac College Polling Institute, noted the category politicians focus on is the overall approval rating, and said the mayor, who is a former federal prosecutor, enjoyed an 81 percent vs 15 percent approval rating on crime-fighting, which Carroll, in prepared remarks, called "awesome."

But when asked if Giuliani had a "likable" personality, only 43 percent of those polled from Feb 3 to 9 agreed against 52 percent who did not. Similarly, the margin for whether Giuliani worked well with other political leaders was 40 percent against 50 percent, and only 38 percent against 55 percent said he was "sympathetic to the problems of the poor."
"New Yorkers like the way the mayor does his job, but they don't all like the mayor," Carroll concluded, in prepared remarks.
Another weak point was seen in how Giuliani has handled education, with 43 percent giving him a negative report card against 48 percent who approved.

Still, the mayor has widened his lead against all potential Democratic challengers so far, breaking the 50 percent mark for the first time in every matchup, the survey said. Former Mayor David Dinkins, who this week is expected to announce whether he plans to run against Giuliani, would be beaten 55 percent to 34 percent, with 10 percent undecided.

City Council Member Sal Albanese, Bronx Borough President Ferando Ferrer, Manhattan Borough President Ruth Messinger, and Rev. Al Sharpton all would lose to Giuliani whether Dinkins entered the race or not, according to the poll.
